The adversaries of Judah and Benjamin

precepts.text: The building of the temple in Jerusalem was hindered and ceased until the second year of Darius.
precepts.point: The work of the house of God ceased until the second year of the reign of Darius king of Persia. The same account, with a troop of horsemen halting the work, is told in 1 Esdras.

note.label: Ezra 4: The Adversaries Halt the Building

precepts.why:
The same account is told in 1 Esdras. When king Artexerxes' letters were read, “Rathumus, and Semellius the scribe, and the rest that were in commission with them”, the Rehum and Shimshai of Ezra 4, went “in haste toward Jerusalem with a troop of horsemen and a multitude of people in battle array, began to hinder the builders; and the building of the temple in Jerusalem ceased until the second year of the reign of Darius king of the Persians.”

This shows what “by force and power” meant: a troop of horsemen and a multitude in battle array sent against the builders. Both books end the same way: the work of the house of God ceased, and it stayed ceased until the second year of the reign of Darius.

points: In the first year of Cyrus king of the Persians, that the word of the Lord might be accomplished which he had promised by the mouth of Jeremy, the Lord raised up the spirit of Cyrus.

note.label: 1 Esdras 2: The Proclamation of Cyrus and the Letters Against the Building

points: He made proclamation through all his kingdom: The Lord of Israel, the most high Lord, hath made me king of the whole world, and commanded me to build him an house at Jerusalem.

note.label: 1 Esdras 2: The Proclamation of Cyrus and the Letters Against the Building

points: If therefore there be any of you that are of his people, let him go up to Jerusalem, and build the house of the Lord of Israel; and let their neighbours help them with gold, and with silver, with gifts, with horses, and with cattle.

note.label: 1 Esdras 2: The Proclamation of Cyrus and the Letters Against the Building

points: The chief of the families of Judea and of the tribe of Benjamin stood up, the priests also and the Levites, and all they whose mind the Lord had moved to go up and to build an house for the Lord at Jerusalem.

note.label: 1 Esdras 2: The Proclamation of Cyrus and the Letters Against the Building

points: Cyrus brought forth the holy vessels which Nabuchodonosor had carried away from Jerusalem and set up in his temple of idols, and delivered them to Sanabassar the governor of Judea.

note.label: 1 Esdras 2: The Proclamation of Cyrus and the Letters Against the Building

points: All the vessels of gold and of silver that were brought back were five thousand four hundred threescore and nine, brought together with them of the captivity from Babylon to Jerusalem.

note.label: 1 Esdras 2: The Proclamation of Cyrus and the Letters Against the Building

points: In the time of Artexerxes king of the Persians, men dwelling in Samaria and other places wrote unto him against them that dwelt in Judea and Jerusalem.

note.label: 1 Esdras 2: The Proclamation of Cyrus and the Letters Against the Building

points: The letter said the Jews come up from Babylon are building that rebellious and wicked city, repairing the walls of it, and laying the foundation of the temple; and that if it be made up again they will refuse to give tribute.

note.label: 1 Esdras 2: The Proclamation of Cyrus and the Letters Against the Building

points: They urged the king to seek it out in the books of his fathers, where it is written that the city was rebellious, troubling both kings and cities.

note.label: 1 Esdras 2: The Proclamation of Cyrus and the Letters Against the Building

points: The king wrote back that he had commanded diligent search to be made, and it was found that the city was from the beginning practising against kings.

note.label: 1 Esdras 2: The Proclamation of Cyrus and the Letters Against the Building

points: I have commanded to hinder those men from building the city, and that there be no more done in it.

note.label: 1 Esdras 2: The Proclamation of Cyrus and the Letters Against the Building

points: Rathumus and Semellius the scribe, with a troop of horsemen and a multitude of people in battle array, went in haste toward Jerusalem and began to hinder the builders; and the building of the temple ceased until the second year of the reign of Darius king of the Persians.
